audit_source:
import JSP121Main

/- Scope audit only; all mathematical construction remains attributed upstream.
   JSP121Main is a byte-identical copy of the pinned original entry source,
   placed at a leaf module name to avoid prefix-based multi-module replay. -/
open Filter Set

namespace JSP121Audit

/-- Literal original quantifiers, including exact aleph-one chromatic number,
    a graph-dependent eventual threshold, and arbitrary finite subgraphs. -/
def CatalogClaim : Prop :=
  ∃ F : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ X : Erdos110.BundledGraph,
    (Nonempty (X.graph.Coloring (Set.Iio (Ordinal.omega.{0} 1))) ∧
      IsEmpty (X.graph.Coloring ℕ)) →
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ H : X.graph.Subgraph,
        H.verts.Finite ∧ H.verts.ncard ≤ F n ∧
          H.coe.chromaticNumber = n

theorem catalog_claim_false : ¬ CatalogClaim := Erdos110.not_erdos_110

/-- Counterexamples fail a proposed bound at arbitrarily late targets.
    This statement does not claim the stronger full quantitative paper theorem. -/
theorem arbitrarily_late_counterexamples (F : ℕ → ℕ) :
    ∃ X : Erdos110.BundledGraph,
      (Nonempty (X.graph.Coloring (Set.Iio (Ordinal.omega.{0} 1))) ∧
        IsEmpty (X.graph.Coloring ℕ)) ∧
      ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n : ℕ, N ≤ n ∧
        ∀ H : X.graph.Subgraph,
          H.verts.Finite → H.verts.ncard ≤ F n →
            H.coe.chromaticNumber ≠ n :=
  Erdos110.lambieHansonConclusion F

end JSP121Audit

# JSP-000121 / Erdős 110: scope and local verification review

The source covers the original negative answer. Actual local verification completed on 2026-09-16: all 17 compilations and 16 explicit single-leaf replays exited 0 and passed the strict receipt checks. All five named axiom declarations report exactly `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. This scope assessment and same-kernel local reproduction do not constitute official verification or an independent checker implementation.

The [original statement](https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/110) asks for one function F such that every graph of chromatic number exactly ℵ₁ has, for every sufficiently large n, a subgraph of chromatic number exactly n on at most F(n) vertices. The eventual threshold may depend on the graph. The [Lambie-Hanson paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.08177) proves a stronger all-target slow-growth theorem; the distinction below matters when describing this formalization.

The pinned `HasUniformBound` preserves the order of quantifiers: one F, then every bundled graph, then an eventual assertion in n. It does not permit F to depend on the graph and does not demand a single threshold shared by all graphs. Subgraphs are arbitrary Mathlib subgraphs, not just induced subgraphs. Explicit `H.verts.Finite` prevents `Set.ncard` on an infinite vertex set from giving a false small-size witness. The target is the actual chromatic number of the finite subgraph, not merely a chosen coloring.

`IsAlephOneChromatic G` requires a coloring by ordinals below ω₁ and the absence of a coloring by ℕ. These two conditions represent exact chromatic number ℵ₁. The vertex set is not required to have cardinality ℵ₁. The concrete witness lives in `Type 1`, so it suffices to refute a purported bound applying to all graphs; fixing that universe does not weaken the counterexample. This package does not claim a graph on exactly ℵ₁ vertices.

The source constructs its height system on a stationary slice of cofinality κ = ℵ₁ below λ = ℵ₃. `Height.exists_clubGuessing` discharges its club-guessing input through the imported, proved PCF construction and the regularity/cofinality lemmas. No CH, diamond, forcing extension, or unproved club-guessing premise appears in the final theorem. The source explicitly calls this a variant of the published construction; we do not claim identity with every detail of the paper's witness.

For each proposed F, the actual theorem uses targets `t(k)=2^(k+1)+1` and `q(k)=F(t(k))`. `FiniteEstimate.chromaticNumber_le` bounds the chromatic number of every finite subgraph with at most q(k) vertices by `2^(k+1)`. The graph itself admits an ω₁-coloring but no natural-number coloring. Given any threshold N, choosing k=N gives t(k)≥N and defeats F at that target. Thus failures are arbitrarily late, which is exactly what is needed to negate an eventual bound. No monotonicity assumption on F is added.

The proven endpoint is `Erdos110.lambieHansonConclusion`, followed by `Erdos110.not_erdos_110` and its alias `Erdos110.erdos_110`. In contrast, `LambieHansonTheorem` is only a `def Prop` in this snapshot, with a lemma saying that this stronger proposition would imply the endpoint. There is no proof here of that stronger statement for every n≥3. The public scope must therefore remain the complete original disproof, not formalization of the entire stronger quantitative theorem.

The source's referenced `tex/110.tex` is absent from the pinned checkout and was not used as evidence. The checked source closure consists of 15 files and 3,246 lines; its external imports are all Mathlib modules. Static inspection found no proof placeholders or custom axiom declarations. All 15 unchanged source files were actually compiled. The original parent module was compile-only; its exact source bytes were additionally compiled and replayed as the separate leaf `JSP121Main`, and `Audit` imports only that leaf. The 16 replays cover the 14 original leaf modules, `JSP121Main`, and `Audit`, with exactly one reported target each. The alias is not claimed to have the original module identity or compiled binary. The five axiom reports cover the original endpoint and alias, the witness conclusion, and both explicit typed-audit statements. Imported Mathlib, package and standard-library artifacts remain trusted. The complete logs, source/plan hashes, compilation-receipt bindings, and unchanged output-bundle inventories are embedded in `public-evidence.json`; every operation records `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1`.

The source credits Chris Lambie-Hanson for the mathematics, Codex / GPT-5.6 Sol for the formalization, and separately carries a 2026 Boris Alexeev copyright notice with “Authors: OpenAI Codex.” Five PCF files retain attribution to Y. Paz's `PCF-Theory` adaptations and Apache-2.0 notices. All of these credits are preserved without claiming new authorship or adjudicating author history. The public package links the original sources instead of redistributing their bodies.
